feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is slightly repetitive and could be tightened to sharpen impact and reduce overlap across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and credibility markers: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms strengthen impact.  
- Well-aligned positioning: headline, summary, competencies, and project examples consistently support the target brand of digital platform and communications systems leader.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: include improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, conversion, or cost/time savings where possible.  
- Minor style/consistency edits: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation style varies in lists; “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “Native” / “A2 (learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar issues.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce repetition: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add scale or outcome where possible to increase impact, e.g., “supporting complex, mission-driven organizations serving large audiences and multi-publisher teams.”
- Replace the slightly generic “building the platforms” with stronger verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Consider a cleaner second sentence: “Leads web modernization, editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward senior, recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing to parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing systems, functions, and outputs.
- Emphasize higher-level leadership scope over tactical execution where possible.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If targeting more technical roles, swap “Public-sector advocacy communications” for “CMS and content platform delivery” to better complement recent Drupal/search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this block broad and avoid repeating channel details elsewhere.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Strengthen specificity with scale or outcome where possible: e.g., audience served, campaign purpose, conference/event context, or organizational impact.
- Standardize style: use consistent verb tense, serial commas, and hyphenation; change “10×20-foot” to “10 x 20-foot” for readability.
- Sharpen wording: “bill-level AI chat” could become “bill-specific AI chat,” and “continued campaign growth” could become “future campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- Consider keeping only the most distinctive projects here, especially the anniversary campaign/display, which adds new texture.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive recent deliverables and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic bullets with outcome-led ones, e.g. “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, including downloadable member toolkits, to support advocacy and member engagement.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance language: “Improved cross-channel content operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the AI/search bullet more concrete: include scope, users, content volume, or expected impact on findability, self-service, or editorial efficiency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement” repeats the header summary and core competencies.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new here: consulting model, AI search, and specific Drupal builds.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management language is reduced to avoid overlap with the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia operations, leading enterprise web modernization and cross-channel communications for a national association.”
- Recast bullets to emphasize transformation and scale: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, engagement lift, reporting time saved, production cost reduction, faster publishing, or improved stakeholder adoption.
- Tighten phrasing: combine governance/planning/standards into one operations bullet and avoid listing every platform unless tied to a result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with older video-production bullets; frame it here as capacity-building and operational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about hands-on operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the broader strategic remit of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.
- Combine the last two bullets for concision: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the later Director role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on launching/scaling it, not owning the full video program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” to sound more operational and leadership-focused.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “for high-volume, multi-stakeholder organizations” to reinforce scale.
- Keep terms aligned with recent roles: prioritize governance, enterprise web, and cross-channel leadership over broader editorial wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to experience bullets on editorial planning; avoid repeating that exact idea elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Consider dropping lower-priority platforms unless central to target roles; “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” can be grouped as “additional CMS platforms.”
- If space allows, add one proof point in adjacent experience instead of here, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page site” or “AI search for legislative/policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” from Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool detail is already covered in Technical + IT; avoid listing the same stack twice verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • Web performance and SEO analysis • User behavior insights • Dashboard development (GA4, Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery)”
- Put strategic skills first; keep tools in parentheses or at the end.
- Replace “optimization” with a clearer outcome-oriented term like “user behavior insights” or “performance measurement” unless you can cite testing/CRO elsewhere.
- If space allows, align wording to recent experience: “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” entry in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video and livestream production for advocacy, studio and hybrid event environments.”
- Tighten and group related items: “Video production & post-production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems.”
- If space allows, add scale/ownership from recent roles: “Built and operated an in-house studio; supported recurring advocacy programming and virtual/hybrid events.”
- Consider replacing “virtual event production” with “broadcast-quality studio production” to better reflect the NACo studio build and seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase here.
- Tool-level detail overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” in Technical + IT, so keep this section focused on higher-level capabilities.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeat generic CMS names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: **Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider tightening the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- Best upgrade: replace this list with a more outcome-linked version, e.g. **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or making this version more specific to platform depth.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the rest unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior candidate.
- Consider replacing “API integrations” with “REST/API integrations” or “API-based workflow integration” for sharper technical specificity.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end implementation for Drupal” or “deployment automation,” rather than expanding the list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating identical phrasing.
- GTM overlaps with analytics infrastructure themes elsewhere, so keep this item focused on implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. Since “workflow automation and platform integration” already appears elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a qualifier to show depth: “used to build intake, approval, publishing, and cross-team coordination workflows”
- Keep only the strongest/recently relevant tools; consider dropping Basecamp or Trello if they were secondary compared with Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools, so don’t let them take equal weight with actual automation platforms

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform breadth and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier for level of use: **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member communications**
- Best stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (automation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (campaign/newsletter delivery)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Your work experience already covers email/newsletter leadership; don’t add phrases like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here.
- If Higher Logic was your primary NACo platform, consider listing it first to better align with recent experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic list rather than a differentiated technical capability section. Tighten it and emphasize tools over broad functions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing frameworks
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with specific platforms or methods; if no specific SEO tool is used, use “SEO analysis” instead.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools from the NACo role: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this stack to outcomes in recent roles instead of here, e.g., reporting infrastructure, decision support, or optimization gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with Looker Studio and Power BI, so it adds little value.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundation-building role: team formation, early channel operations, and concrete production output.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team, establishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes: mention the website refresh, recurring livestream/video production, and any volume/frequency metrics if available (e.g., number of livestreams, weekly series duration, audience growth).
- Tighten phrasing by replacing “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables: “produced livestreams, weekly video updates and other digital content supporting advocacy and member communications.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped supervise…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive “firsts,” cross-functional coordination, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for county-facing programs, while expanding NACo’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with specific deliverables if possible: web stories, videos, interviews, reports, or campaign assets.
- Add scale/outcomes if available: number of episodes, audiences served, program teams supported, or how content supported advocacy/member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Keep this entry focused on innovation/research coordination + first podcast launch, not general digital operations.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it so it reads as a tools list, with only the most relevant production capabilities retained.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as primarily software/platforms, not broad functions.
- Use more specific, current phrasing: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- Replace vague wording with tighter capability labels only if needed: “Livestream studio operations” instead of “Livestream studio workflows”
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio operations • Podcast recording/editing”
